player_0.content: New plan: I incorrectly identified the sentence as ambiguous because I failed to apply the standard grammatical convention of proximity. In English, when a pronoun has multiple potential antecedents, the one closest to the pronoun is the default interpretation unless context suggests otherwise. In this sentence, "she" is immediately followed by "had," and the subject of the main clause ("The patient") is the only logical entity capable of having a skin condition that necessitates a referral. The specialist is the recipient of the referral, not the subject of the reason clause. My strategy should be to first check for the nearest noun before considering syntactic ambiguity; if the nearest noun makes logical sense, the sentence is not ambiguous.
